sentence: This project builds physical models and machine learning methods to simulate how proteins and other biomolecules move and change shape.
This project studies how changes to proteins in the brain after heroin use in rats lead to relapse after drug withdrawal.
This project tries to find out which human genes raise the risk of coronary artery disease and how those genes work.
This project works to reduce cancer incidence and mortality by translating knowledge from basic and population health discoveries to at-risk populations.
This project studies whether an enzyme called histone deacetylase helps melanoma cells resist drugs and escape attack by the immune system.
This project studies how hematopoietic stem cells move out of the blood and into the bone marrow after transplantation.
This project studies how normal stem cells and cancer cells grow, change and are controlled, and how the surrounding microenvironment affects tumor formation.
This project studies how cells fuse to form cells with many nuclei and how those nuclei help the body work.
This project builds engineered T cell therapy in mouse models of glioblastoma and tries to find out why some tumors escape it.
This project uses large genomic datasets to study how mobile element insertions in DNA are linked to neurological disease.
This project studies how viruses, bacteria and the immune system interact to affect the risk of type 2 diabetes.
This project tries to find out how a class of non-coding RNAs is controlled and how it helps cells make ribosomes and proteins.
This project compares two filoviruses to find out how a viral protein changes ubiquitination in host cells.
This project studies basic principles of cancer immunobiology and works on cancer treatments.
This project studies how risk genes lead to autism spectrum disorder and schizophrenia by testing human glutamatergic neurons with changes in those genes.
This project manages and analyzes large data on how the immune system develops in infants at high risk or low risk for allergic disease.
This project tries to predict which patients will get acute kidney injury after surgery by combining genetic information with electronic health records.
This project studies how the retina sends visual signals to the superior colliculus in rat and primate animal models.
This project studies how cardiomyocytes, endothelial cells and cardiac fibroblasts signal each other in a type of inherited heart disease.
This project improves methods for editing genes in T cells and hematopoietic stem cells and measures off-target editing.
